chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il al-Mithamī narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn 'Ali, from some of our companions, from al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said:
«The elder brother is in the position of the father.»
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of an elder brother in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on marriage guardianship, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the elder brother as the primary male guardian (wali) in the absence of the father, reflecting the patriarchal structure of Shia family law. This ruling is crucial for determining the validity of marriage contracts for minors, particularly orphans, and underscores the ethical responsibility of senior siblings to act as paternal figures.
